transitions.use: 685.6 nm (air; 685.79 nm vac): closed (cycling) transition from the metastable 3s 4P5/2 level; suggested for laser cooling of metastable fluorine (Shimizu et al., Appl. Phys. B 72, 227 (2001)); optical pumping on it demonstrated in a fast F beam for nuclear-spin polarization (Levy et al. 2007); LIF line of the metastable-lifetime measurement (F=3 -> F'=4 component, Shimizu et al. 2006)

frequency_THz.source: hyperfine centre of gravity 14581.684 cm^-1 from Liden, Ark. Fys. 1, 229 (1949), as quoted and used for calibration in Levy, Cocolios, Behr, Jayamanna, Minamisono, Pearson, Nucl. Instrum. Methods A 580, 1571 (2007), Table 1 (collinear fast-beam LIF and modulated optical depopulation pumping)
frequency_THz.note: derived unit conversion of 14581.684 cm^-1 (vacuum wavenumber as printed); uncertainty is the 150 MHz accuracy Levy et al. attribute to Liden. NIST level difference: 14581.68 cm^-1.

transitions.note: hyperfine structure (19F, I=1/2): lower level A = 2643(1) MHz, upper level A = 1564(1) MHz (Levy et al. 2007); cycling component F=3 -> F'=4; NIST A = 4.87e7 s^-1 (accuracy C+)

transitions.label: 2p4(3P)3s 4P5/2 - 2p4(3P)3p 4D°5/2
transitions.use: 677.4 nm (air; 677.59 nm vac): open transition used for optical depopulation pumping of the metastable 3s 4P5/2 level (upper level also decays to 3s 4P3/2, which decays to the ground state); measurement of the metastable fraction of a neutralized F beam (Levy et al. 2007)

transitions.note: the measured absolute frequency could not be read (paper paywalled); Levy et al. 2007 state that its centre of gravity differs from the Liden (1949) value by 550 MHz

conflicts: Lifetime of metastable 3s 4P5/2: 7.3(5) us (Shimizu et al. 2006) versus 3.7(5) us (Shimizu et al. 2001), same group; the later value is the entry.

Ground 2P°3/2 hyperfine A: 2009.99(1) MHz as tabulated by Aourir et al. (attributed to Radford et al. 1961) versus 2010.005(10) MHz from halving the interval 4020.01(2) MHz printed in the Radford abstract (difference presumably the second-order off-diagonal correction; not verified).
3s 2P hyperfine A: Tate & Aturaliye 1737.1(4) / 3057.9(21) MHz versus Huo et al. 1550(200) / 3048(10) MHz (consistent, less precise).

3s 2P - 3p 2D° line positions: Tate & Aturaliye (1997) differ from Liden (1949) by 550 MHz for the 2P1/2 - 2D°3/2 centre of gravity (statement in Levy et al. 2007; numbers not read). Hocker (1978) reported negative 3p 2D° hyperfine splittings, Liden and Tate positive ones (arXiv:1307.0404).
3d 4P1/2 and 4P5/2 hyperfine A: experiment -226(50) and -17(10) MHz versus theory -445 and -48 MHz (arXiv:2108.01116; attributed there to cancellation effects in the calculation).
not_found: Radiative lifetimes of the 3p, 3s 2P, 3s 2D, 3d levels (beam-foil or LIF): no measurement located.

Hyperfine constants of 3s 4P3/2, 3s 4P1/2, 3p 4S°3/2, 3p 4D°3/2, 3p 4D°1/2, 3p 4P°5/2, 3p 4P°1/2, 3p 2S°, 3p 2P°, 3s 2D, 3d 2F7/2, 3d 4F9/2: no measurement (arXiv:1804.03952 and 2108.01116 state that none exists for several of these; theory only). Huo et al. 2018 may contain further 3p values; paper not open.
Absolute frequency of the 780 nm 3s 2P1/2 - 3p 2D°3/2 hyperfine component (Tate & Aturaliye 1997): abstract opened, number is in the paywalled text.
Isotope shifts: 19F is the only stable isotope; no radioactive-isotope optical data located.
Measured transition probabilities newer than NIST for the 3s-3p lines: none located.

Shimizu et al., Appl. Phys. B 72, 227 (2001) (laser-cooling proposal for the 685.6 nm line): not opened; the proposal and its 3.7(5) us lifetime are second-hand from Levy et al. 2007. No demonstrated laser cooling or trapping of F was located.
Final g_J(2P°3/2) as printed by Radford et al. 1961: only the ratio to the proton g factor is in the abstract; the entry is derived.
Lande g factors of excited levels: none located.
notes: Level energies are NIST ASD values. 19F: I = 1/2, so only magnetic-dipole constants A exist (no B). The 3d-level A values (Huo et al. 2018) are second-hand from the theory paper arXiv:2108.01116 and carry about 5 % uncertainty. Lifetime of the metastable 3s 4P5/2 level: the Elsevier text of Levy et al. prints the unit with a symbol-font glyph ("ms"); it is microseconds, as the abstract of Shimizu et al. 2006 states explicitly (7.3 +- 0.5 us). The frequency of the 685.6 nm line is an old (1949) value quoted second-hand; treat it as a consistency check of the NIST Ritz value, not as a precision measurement. Sources were located through arXiv/DataCite, CORE, HAL, Crossref and publisher abstract pages; the web-search quota of the session was exhausted, so coverage is limited to what those indexes exposed.
